title: Analyzing Cellular Internalization of Nanoparticles and Bacteria by Multi-spectral Imaging Flow Cytometry
protocol: Harvest RAW 264.7 cells from their flasks when they reach confluency by scraping gently with a cell scraper.
Count and plate harvested RAW 264.7 cells into a 24-well cell culture dish at a density of 5 x 10^5 cells/well in 0.5 mL complete Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (cDMEM).
Incubate the plated cells overnight at 37 °C in a 5% CO2 incubator.
Introduce recombinant plasmids expressing green fluorescent protein (GFP) to S. Typhimurium by electroporation.
Prepare a culture of Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (ATCC 14028) in LB broth and incubate overnight at 37 °C with aeration.
Pellet 1 mL of the bacteria at maximum speed in a microcentrifuge.
Wash the cells four times with 1 mL of cold MOPS/glycerol solution by gently resuspending the pellet between each wash.
Resuspend the final washed pellet in 50 μL of MOPS/glycerol containing ~0.5 μg of pAKgfp1 or pAKgfplux1 plasmid DNA.
Transfer the cell suspension to a pre-chilled 1 mm gap electroporation cuvette.
Electroporate using settings: 1800 V, 200 W, 25 mF.
Add 1 mL of LB broth immediately after pulse delivery and transfer the cell suspension to a new 15 mL tube.
Allow the cells to recover at 37 °C with aeration for one hour.
Concentrate the cells by centrifugation and resuspend in ~100 μL of remaining supernatant.
Plate the cells on LB plates containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Purify single colonies by restreaking with antibiotic selection.
Confirm expression of GFP by illumination with a standard fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) filter set.
Inoculate 10 mL of LB broth containing 25 μg/mL ampicillin with a loopful of Salmonella that has been transformed to stably express GFP.
Grow the bacteria overnight at 37 °C.
Dilute Salmonella 1:10 into a fresh culture tube containing 10 mL LB supplemented with ampicillin and incubate for 5 h at 37 °C.
Measure the absorbance of the culture at 600 nm.
Calculate the concentration of the Salmonella per mL using a previously established growth curve.
Dilute the Salmonella in cDMEM (0.5 mL/well) to obtain a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 100 per RAW 264.7 cell.
Fabricate 1% FITC-loaded nanoparticles by dissolving polymer in methylene chloride (4 °C, concentration 25 mg/mL).
Precipitate the polymer mixture in pentane (-30 °C) with a ratio of 1:200 methylene chloride to pentane.
Recover nanoparticles by vacuum filtration and evaporate any residual solvent.
Weigh the dried polyanhydride nanoparticles using sterilized weigh paper.
Add 5 mg of nanoparticles to 0.5 mL cold phosphate buffered saline (PBS, calcium and magnesium free, pH 7.4).
Keep nanoparticle suspension on ice until use.
Sonicate the nanoparticle suspension for approximately 25 s at 4 to 6 joules while keeping it on ice.
Pretreat a subset of RAW 264.7 cells with 5 μg/mL cytochalasin-D for 1 hr by replacing medium with fresh cDMEM supplemented with inhibitor.
Return the cultures to 37 °C incubator after pretreatment.
Vortex the nanoparticle suspension and add 10 μL to appropriate wells after the 1 h incubation.
Incubate at 37 °C or 4 °C (control) for 45 min after adding nanoparticles.
Remove the plates from the incubator or refrigerator and place on ice.
Wash the cells twice with ice cold PBS (without Ca2+ and Mg2+) by aspirating and discarding the old medium.
Add 250 μL of ice-cold PBS to harvested wells and gently scrape the wells.
Pipet the harvested cells into clear-view snap cap microcentrifuge tubes and keep them on ice.
Wash the cells by adding 1 mL of cold wash buffer (2% heat inactivated FBS, 0.1% sodium azide in PBS) and centrifuge at 250 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and remove residual buffer by tapping the inverted microcentrifuge tube on paper towel.
Resuspend the cell pellet by gently raking the microcentrifuge tube across a test tube rack.
Fix the RAW 264.7 cells by adding 100 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS and allow the cells to stand for 15 min at room temperature (RT).
Wash the RAW 264.7 cells by adding 1 mL of Perm/Wash buffer (BD Biosciences) and centrifuge at 250 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Repeat step 4.9.
Stain the RAW 264.7 cells for actin by adding 100 μl of Perm/Wash buffer containing Alexa Fluor phalloidin 660 (AF 660; 1:150 dilution) for 15 min at RT.
Repeat steps 4.11 and 4.12.
Resuspend RAW 264.7 cells in 50 μL of PBS containing 1% PFA.
Store the resuspended cells in the dark at 4 °C until acquisition.
Power up ImageStreamX and launch INSPIRE.
Initialize Fluidics.
Load Default Template in the file menu.
Select ALL in the Image Gallery view menu.
Press Run Setup to start imaging the beads.
Adjust Core Tracking to center images laterally (if necessary).
Select the Brightfield (BF) channel and click Set Intensity.
Wait until the Flow Speed CV is consistently less than 0.2%.
Calibrate the instrument daily.
Click Start All in the ASSIST tab to run calibrations and tests.
Verify that all tests have passed.
Press Flush Lock and Load (FLL) to load the first sample.
Load the brightest sample in the experiment that fluoresces with each fluorochrome used.
Turn on each laser used in the experiment.
Set Laser Power so each fluorochrome has max pixel values between 100 and 4000 counts.
Set Cell Classification criteria to eliminate collection of unwanted objects.
Select the Area Lower Limit in BF channel to 50 μm.
Enter the File Name, Destination Folder, set Sequence # to 1 and the Number of Events to acquire.
Click Run Acquire to collect and save the first experiment data file.
Press Flush Lock and Load (FLL) and run the next experimental sample.
Repeat until all experimental samples have been collected.
Click Comp Settings to turn off brightfield and scatter laser and enable collection of all channels.
Collect 500 positive cells from each single stained sample for each fluorophore in the experiment to develop a compensation matrix.
Run the brightest sample first.
Run remaining test samples after the brightest sample.
Collect compensation controls containing single color fluorescence.
Save an INSPIRE template to set instrument settings and reload it as needed.
Use the autosampler for unattended operation with one template for experimental samples and separate templates for each single color control.
Configure ImageStreamX using 488 nm and 658 nm excitation lasers, 785 nm scatter laser, a 40X (0.75 NA) objective, and a 6 channel system with a standard ISX filter stack.
Image nanoparticles with the 488 nm laser at 10 mW, the 658 nm laser at 50 mW, and the 785 nm laser at 2 mW, excluding brightfield (BF) in channel 1.
Image Salmonella infected cells with the 488 nm laser at 20 mW, the 658 nm laser at 50 mW, the 785 nm laser at 2 mW, and BF in channel 1.
Collect compensation controls without brightfield (BF) and 785 nm scatter laser.
Image at least 5000 events (cells) for each test sample.
Launch IDEAS.
Double-click on the Internalization wizard.
Load one of the test sample .rif files.
Create a compensation matrix by clicking 'New Matrix' in step 2.
Add files for the single color controls in the experiment.
Click next through the wizard until the compensation matrix file is saved and loaded into the box in step 2.
Click Next and follow directions until a .daf file is generated.
Set image display properties by selecting Ch 2 (FITC) and Ch 5 (AF 660).
Select CH01 for making the cell boundary and CH02 for nanoparticles or bacteria collected.
Generate a scatter plot of Brightfield Area versus Brightfield Aspect Ratio to define single cells and doublets.
Gate around singlets with an aspect ratio of around 1.
Generate a histogram of the Brightfield Gradient RMS and set the population view in the image gallery to selected bin.
Click on bins to determine where focused cells begin and draw a line region to gate focused cells.
Generate a scatter plot of Intensity of Channel 2 on the x-axis versus Max Pixel of Ch2 on the y-axis.
Click on the dots in the scatter plot to view the images.
Adjust the region around the cells that are positive for nanoparticles or bacteria based on image inspection.
Generate a histogram of the Internalization feature beginning at 0.
Observe images to adjust the Internalization feature manually as necessary.
Create an Object mask on the brightfield image.
Erode this Object mask by 4 pixels to create a new region.
Calculate the Internalization feature based on the eroded Object mask.
Distinguish internalized particles and bacteria from surface-bound ones using the Internalization feature.
Create a new histogram with the Internalization feature based on the eroded Object mask.
Draw a region to gate on internalized cells by viewing the imagery in selected bin mode.
Set the gating threshold at 0.3.
Consider cells with a score lower than 0.3 as surface bound particle positive cells.
Use the IDEAS Spot Count feature to eliminate background labeled cells and identify specific internalized nanoparticles or bacteria.
Define spots using the Mask, Spot, Peak, and Intensity functions.
Find bright details in an image with a specified radius and threshold above local background.
Refine the mask by breaking apart high intensities into individual spots using the Peak function.
Include spots above an intensity of 200 counts.
Generate a statistics report template by including various features in the Reports menu.
Save the file as a template for batch analysis of all experimental files.
In the IDEAS software, click Tools→ Batch Data Files.
Input all the .rif files.
Add the compensation matrix file (.ctm).
Add the template file (.ast).
Submit the batch for processing.
Generate a final report file with statistics for all the samples.
Incubate RAW 264.7 cells with Salmonella at 4 °C to reduce internalization without an apparent increase in surface-bound bacteria compared to the 37 °C control.
Treat RAW 264.7 cells with cytochalasin-D to inhibit actin polymerization and observe a reduction in internalized NP and Salmonella.
Increase the percentage of cells positive for surface-bound NP from approximately 8% at 37 °C to greater than 35% after either cytochalasin-D or 4 °C treatment.
